title.narrative: Local development network created

description.narrative: Local development network created

comment.narrative: The project team prepared the ToR for the Sawyan Network including the objectives of the network Membership criteria Practical information on how to join the network.After the publication of the initial application in early July 2022 130 CSOs expressed their interest in joining the network and 109 out of them were selected. After the completion of logistics and communication materials KP held the kickoff meeting for the network on the 12th of September with the attendance of 93 grassroots civil society organizations youth and women teams in Idleb governorate.On 21st September the Board members were elected taking into account gender and geographic balance in order to ensure the representation of women and all subdistricts. On the 20th of October a monthly meeting of Sawyan Network was held and a final review of the networks ToR was done.Between 20 and 29 of November KP conducted the bimonthly meetings of Sawyan Network in the 8 subdistricts and the total number of participants was 62 CSOs. During these meetings KP presented the latest updates about the network including the ToR of Sawyan network and defined the main challenges to be faced by members work and the top needs in education child protection and livelihoods in the subdistricts.Because of the strong earthquake that struck southeast Turkey and northwest Syria on the 6th February 2023 the meetings of the Network were temporarily suspended. Finally on 30th March the network was able to resume its activities by organizing a meeting with its Board in order to set priorities after the consequences of that natural disaster and to share the latest updates about the subgrants allocation process.On 3rd September 2023 a meeting with all the members of the network was organized in the 8 subdistricts the latest achievements of Sawyan action were shared special focus was also given to the explanation of roles and responsibilities of network members in achieving its agreed goals and finally some of the network members presented their responses to the severe consequences of the earthquake.It should be noted that despite the networks inability to organise regular meetings the connections between its members continued and were crucial in providing a coordinated response to the needs arising from the worsening context due to the additional earthquake crisis. Some of the 51 selected CSOs of the Sawyan action contributed significantly to the collection of data on the basis of which proposals to respond to the ongoing emergency were developed.

title.narrative: People involved in public events

description.narrative: People involved in public events

comment.narrative: During December 2022 the Terms of Reference ToRs for public events were finalized.In August September 2023 the project team achieved the following milestones1. Obtained written approval from local authorities to organize public events.2. Finalized all logistics arrangements with suppliers.3. Held preparatory meetings with Civil Society Organizations CSOs to confirm participants and define presentations.4. Designed invitations shared among CSOs and stakeholdersFrom October 21st to 29th 2023 eight public events were successfully organized in Dana Maaret Mesrin Ariha Idleb Qah and Kafr Takharim in collaboration with ten subgranted CSOs. 15 furnished spaces were rent and PPEs leaflets and refreshments were procured and provided to all participants.Those events engaged a total of 2385 participants among various stakeholders community leaders activists and local authorities. The discussions at these events focused on critical issues such as community participation unemployment vocational learnings impact on societal development vocational improvement for Persons with Disabilities PWD and the role of society in supporting these efforts. Furthermore the events highlighted the significant achievements of the Sawyan action and showcased the 10 selected projects.Additionally two online public events were conducted in collaboration with the CSO Together to Build the Country. The first one was held on 30th November 2023 and reached a total of 778 467 M 311 F participants while the second event held on 4th December 2023 reached a total of 493 279 M 214 F. To be noted that this last event as well was meant to be held at the end of November 2023 but technical difficulties caused an interruption forcing us to reschedule the event at the beginning of December. These online events targeted university students professors intellectuals and researchers focusing on the key accomplishments of the Sawyan action and addressing challenges faced by young graduates in Northwest Syria such as skills gaps and limited job opportunities.Overall the ten events engaged a total of 3656 participants 2010 M and 1646 F. Activity 2.1 under Action 2.

description.narrative: CSOs present their communitybased projects

comment.narrative: During November and December 2022 we worked on defining the top needs and priorities in a consultative process. we sent an email to FSL Education Child Protection and Early Recovery clusters and got their inputs based on available secondary data resources. Based on this we mapped the needs also directly from Sawyan network members to be used as an evidence base in preparing the allocation paper. During the second half of December 2022 and early January 2023 we defined the eligibility criteria introducing them in a meeting in 11 December to the representatives of 51 CSOs. The team then selected 33 eligible CSOs who could apply directly to small grants allocation and prepared the draft allocation paper along with its annexes list of indicators proposal template budget template and translated them into Arabic.On 9 January 2023 KP launched the allocation paper and shared with all 51 CSOs in Sawyan project. To achieve this we organized 2 information sessions one on 11 January to explain all details of the allocation and answer any questions. Another meeting was conducted on 18 January to answer the questions of CSOs who were planning to apply. The deadline for application was set on the 31 of January 2023. In the meantime KP prepared the scoring and established the evaluation committee.

comment.narrative: The preparations for the provision of training were finalized in mid of May 2022 including contracting with training company contracting with the service company for the provision of venues and logistics of training developing the training implementation plan that included the start and end dates of each training package in each location and the names of trainees and trainers through the established communication channels WhatsApp groups. An assessment framework has also been developed to be able to measure improvements in competencies and project impact Training commenced with the provision of Internal Governance Program PCM Project cycle management in 15 May 2022 and then continued with the provision of Human Resources and Financial Management and EuropeAid financing mechanism and grant management on 16 July and finally the Sphere handbook minimum standards and principles of humanitarian action started in 11 September.The five training packages were completed in 2 November 2022 453 trainees 287 men 166 women including managerial staff from 51 CSOs were trained on Internal Governance Programme PCM Project cycle management Human Resources and Financial Management EuropeAid financing mechanism and grant management in addition to Sphere handbook minimum standards and principles of humanitarian action. During the period 14 to 29 November 2022 KP conducted another training round for the trainees who did not have the chance to join in the original period. These sessions reached 60 additional trainees to increase the total number reached in this activity to 513 316 men 197 women as indicated in the dashboard below. The approach including an assessment of competency to measure the impact of the training on new skills and knowledge. The overall rate of improvement for all trainees was 62 Pretest average was 30.1 and posttest average was 91.7KPs media team has designed the certificates of attendance for all trainees who participated in the training packages in the original period and to the new trainees reached in the second round. Additionally certificates were awarded to each CSO to be used as reference letter and distributed in January in small ceremonies with media coverage. The liaison officer has shared directly ecopies of certificates to all trainees.

comment.narrative: On 25 August KP contracted a consultancy company Towards Impact through a competitive process based on quality and cost. The aim was for Towards Impact to conduct an evaluation and review of the available policies of each CSO and develop a set of basic policies. Towards Impact would also provide guidance on how to develop and implement policies to the 51 teams and organizations benefiting from the Sawyan ProjectDuring the period 1827 September the consultancy conducted comprehensive assessment of 44 CSOs online and through field visits and found that 22 CSOs reported they did not have any policies or SOPs in placeThe other 22 CSOs reported having at least having one policy or SOPs in place The company identified a list of CSOs who to see an improvement in their policies and proceduresDuring October 2022 the consultancy team visited 6 selected CSOs and undertook a review and improvement to their policies and procedures based on the needs. During November 2022 the consultancy team developed a set of model policies and procedures including HR policy and manual Finance Policy Procurement and Logistic Policy Monitoring Evaluation Accountability and Learning Policy Media and communication guidance and Project Management proceduresDuring December 2022 the consultancy shared the new model set of policies and procedures with all CSOs in the Sawyan project and organized online orientation sessions to help the organisations understand how to implement the new policies and SOPs effectively they also provided guidance on best practices for using them in their daytoday operations. These sessions included presentations by experts who used examples and provided recommendations for implementation.The orientation sessions were well received by the Sawyan CSOs and many participants reported that they found the presentations to be helpful and informative. They appreciated the opportunity to ask questions and get clarification on any issues that were not clear to them. Overall the sessions were considered to be an important part of the process of helping the organizations develop and implement the new policies and SOPs and they were seen as an important step towards improving the capacity of these organizations.
